title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime is unchanged by principal localizations
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Let $f\in R$ with $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and $g\in S$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$. Let $R_f$ be the localization of $R$ at $f$ and $S_{fg}$ the localization of $S$ at $\varphi(f)g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], with the ring map $R_f\to S_{fg}$, $r/f^n\mapsto \varphi(r)g^n/(\varphi(f)g)^n$, induced by $\varphi$ (it is of finite type), and let $\mathfrak qS_{fg}=\{y/(\varphi(f)g)^n\mid y\in\mathfrak q\}$, a prime ideal of $S_{fg}$. Then $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] if and only if $R_f\to S_{fg}$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak qS_{fg}$.

proof.text: *Notation and the map $R_f\to S_{fg}$.* Put $h=\varphi(f)g\in S$, so $S_{fg}=S_h$; let $\lambda_R:R\to R_f$, $\lambda_S:S\to S_h$ be the localization maps [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. In $S_h$ the element $\lambda_S(\varphi(f))$ is a unit with inverse $g/h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] applied to $\lambda_S\circ\varphi:R\to S_h$ there is a unique ring map $\varphi':R_f\to S_h$ with $\varphi'(r/1)=\varphi(r)/1$, namely $\varphi'(r/f^n)=\varphi(r)\,(\varphi(f)/1)^{-n}=\varphi(r)g^n/h^n$; this is the map of the statement, and $\varphi'\circ\lambda_R=\lambda_S\circ\varphi$. *$\varphi'$ is of finite type* [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]: if $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $S$ as an $R$-algebra, every element of $S_h$ is $y/h^m=(y/1)(1/h)^m$ with $y=P(s_1,\dots,s_n)$, $P$ a polynomial with coefficients in $R$, so $y/1=P^{\varphi'}(s_1/1,\dots,s_n/1)$ with coefficients $\varphi'(r/1)$, and $s_1/1,\dots,s_n/1,1/h$ generate $S_h$ as an $R_f$-algebra.

proof.text: *A ring map $\theta:F_{\bar h}\to F'$.* Regard $F'$ as an $R$-algebra through $R\xrightarrow{\lambda_R}R_f\to F'$. The ring maps $a_1=j'\circ\lambda_S:S\to F'$ and $a_2=\iota'\circ\sigma:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F'$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras: $a_1\circ\varphi=j'\circ\varphi'\circ\lambda_R$ is the structure map of $F'$ (step 1, and $j'\circ\varphi'$ is the $R_f$-structure map of $F'$), and $\sigma$ is an $R$-algebra map (step 2) while $\iota'$ is an $R_f$-algebra map. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2) over $R$ there is a ring homomorphism $\alpha:F\to F'$ with $\alpha(s\otimes\mu)=(s/1)\otimes\sigma(\mu)$. Then $\alpha(\bar h)=j'(h/1)$ is a unit of $F'$, since $h/1$ is a unit of $S_h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] there is a ring map $\theta:F_{\bar h}\to F'$ with $\theta(x/1)=\alpha(x)$; in particular $\theta(\lambda_F(j(s)))=j'(s/1)$ and $\theta(\lambda_F(\iota(\mu)))=\iota'(\sigma(\mu))$.

proof.text: *A ring map $\beta:F'\to F_{\bar h}$.* By step 3 the image of $f$ under $R\to F\xrightarrow{\lambda_F}F_{\bar h}$ is a unit, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] gives a unique ring map $\rho:R_f\to F_{\bar h}$ with $\rho(r/1)=\lambda_F(r\cdot1_F)$; this makes $F_{\bar h}$ an $R_f$-algebra. (i) $\lambda_F\circ j:S\to F_{\bar h}$ sends $h$ to the unit $\lambda_F(\bar h)$, so the same lemma gives $b_1:S_h\to F_{\bar h}$ with $b_1(s/1)=\lambda_F(j(s))$. It is an $R_f$-algebra map: $b_1\circ\varphi'$ and $\rho$ agree on every $r/1$ ($b_1(\varphi(r)/1)=\lambda_F(\varphi(r)\otimes1)=\lambda_F(r\cdot1_F)$), hence are equal by the uniqueness in that lemma. (ii) $b_2=\lambda_F\circ\iota\circ\sigma^{-1}:\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to F_{\bar h}$ is a ring map, and an $R_f$-algebra map: its composite with $R_f\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and $\rho$ agree on every $r/1$ (both give $\lambda_F(r\cdot1_F)$, as $\sigma^{-1}$ and $\iota$ are $R$-algebra maps), hence are equal. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2) over $R_f$ there is a ring homomorphism $\beta:F'\to F_{\bar h}$ with $\beta(t\otimes\nu)=b_1(t)\,b_2(\nu)$.

proof.text: *$\theta$ matches the points.* By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) for $\lambda_F$ (with $W=\{\bar h^k\}$; $\overline{\mathfrak q}\cap W=\emptyset$ by step 3), $\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h}$ is a prime of $F_{\bar h}$ with $\lambda_F^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h})=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. Let $P'=\theta(\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h})$, a prime of $F'$ ($\theta$ is an isomorphism). Then $\lambda_S^{-1}(j'^{-1}(P'))=(j'\lambda_S)^{-1}(P')=(\theta\lambda_Fj)^{-1}(P')=j^{-1}(\lambda_F^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h}))=j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$. The prime $j'^{-1}(P')$ of $S_h$ therefore has $\lambda_S$-contraction $\mathfrak q$, so by (1) of the same lemma for $\lambda_S$ it equals $\mathfrak qS_h=\mathfrak q'$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] for $\varphi':R_f\to S_h$ and $\mathfrak p'$, $P'=\overline{\mathfrak q}'$.

proof.text: *The fibre of $R_f\to S_{fg}$ is homeomorphic to the open $D(\bar h)$ of the fibre of $R\to S$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\lambda_F:\operatorname{Spec}F_{\bar h}\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]: a homeomorphism $c$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\bar h}$ onto the open subset $D(\bar h)=\{Q:\bar h\notin Q\}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F$; on points $c(P)=\lambda_F^{-1}(P)$, so $c(\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h})=\overline{\mathfrak q}$ by step 7, and $\overline{\mathfrak q}\in D(\bar h)$. The ring isomorphism $\theta$ induces the bijection $P'\mapsto\theta^{-1}(P')$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F'$ onto $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\bar h}$, a homeomorphism (it and its inverse $P\mapsto\theta(P)$ carry $V(I)$ to $V(\theta^{-1}(I))$ resp. $V(J)$ to $V(\theta(J))$), sending $\overline{\mathfrak q}'$ to $\overline{\mathfrak q}F_{\bar h}$ by step 7. Composing, $e=c\circ\theta^{-1}:\operatorname{Spec}F'\to D(\bar h)$ is a homeomorphism with $e(\overline{\mathfrak q}')=\overline{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $U=D(\bar h)$, open in $X$ with $\overline{\mathfrak q}\in U$. If $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $X$, then $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}=\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}\cap U$ is open in the subspace $U$; conversely, if $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $U$, it is $U\cap O$ with $O$ open in $X$, an intersection of two opens of $X$, so open in $X$. By the homeomorphism $e$ of step 8, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $U$ iff $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}'\}=e^{-1}(\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\})$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F'$. By [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (applicable to $R_f\to S_{fg}$ by step 1, with the prime $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak qS_{fg}$ over $\mathfrak p'$, and to $R\to S$), $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ iff $R_f\to S_{fg}$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak qS_{fg}$.
